title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning for Firms
summary: An eight-module programme helping firms build credible recovery and wind-down plans, from scenarios and triggers to client asset return, testing and supervisory review.
intro: This training programme equips finance, risk, compliance and board members to build recovery and wind-down plans that work under stress: designing scenarios and triggers, testing recovery options, protecting client assets and evidencing credibility to supervisors.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip firms to produce recovery and wind-down plans that are credible, usable in a crisis and proportionate to the business, rather than documents written once for a supervisor. Participants leave able to design scenarios and triggers, judge which recovery options would really work, plan an orderly solvent wind-down that returns client money and assets, and see their plan the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: Why plans matter, scenario and trigger design, recovery options and their credibility, liquidity and capital in stress, solvent wind-down mechanics, return of client money and assets, operational continuity and critical services, and governance, testing and supervisory review.
Intended Audience: Chief financial officers, chief risk officers and finance and treasury teams at investment firms, payment and e-money institutions, crypto-asset service providers and fund managers
Compliance officers, heads of operations and plan owners responsible for drafting and maintaining recovery and wind-down plans
Executive and non-executive directors who approve the plan and would lead the firm through a crisis
Learning Objectives: Explain why supervisors require recovery and wind-down plans and what makes them credible
Design severe but plausible scenarios, early warning indicators and recovery triggers
Evaluate recovery options for feasibility, timing and value under stress
Plan an orderly solvent wind-down, including the return of client money and assets
Identify the people, systems, suppliers and critical services needed to keep operating through a wind-down
Embed the plan in governance, test it through fire drills and simulations, and evidence it to supervisors
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day workshops. Each module combines a briefing with worked examples and templates, the final module runs a crisis simulation, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's sector and plan.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of finance, risk or compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of recovery or wind-down planning is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
Basel Committee, Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (2008)
ISO 22301:2019, Security and Resilience – Business Continuity Management Systems

modules.title: Why Recovery and Wind-Down Plans Matter
modules.summary: The purpose of recovery and wind-down planning, what supervisors expect of firms across sectors, and the common reasons plans fail when they are needed most.
objectives: Explain the difference between recovery, solvent wind-down and insolvency
Describe supervisory expectations across investment, payments, crypto and fund sectors
Recognise the hallmarks of a plan written for compliance rather than use
syllabus: Recovery, wind-down and resolution: purpose, scope and proportionality
Harm to clients, counterparties and markets from disorderly failure
Lessons from firm failures where plans did not work
What a credible, usable plan looks like

modules.title: Scenario Design, Indicators and Triggers
modules.summary: How to build severe but plausible stress scenarios from the firm's own business model, and set early warning indicators and triggers that prompt action in time.
objectives: Design idiosyncratic, market-wide and combined stress scenarios
Use reverse stress testing to identify what would make the business unviable
Set indicators, thresholds and escalation triggers linked to risk appetite
syllabus: Business model analysis as the starting point for scenarios
Reverse stress testing and points of non-viability
Early warning indicators: capital, liquidity, revenue, client and operational
Calibrating triggers to avoid both false alarms and late action

modules.title: Recovery Options and Their Credibility
modules.summary: Identifying the actions management could take to restore viability, and testing honestly whether each would work in the time available and in the market conditions of the scenario.
objectives: Identify a realistic menu of recovery options
Assess the feasibility, timing, value and dependencies of each option
Challenge optimistic assumptions about parent support and asset sales
syllabus: Capital raising, cost reduction, business and asset disposals
Group and parent support: commitments versus assumptions
Impediments: legal, operational, market and reputational
Mapping options against scenarios to test overall recovery capacity

modules.title: Liquidity and Capital in Stress
modules.summary: How capital and liquidity behave as stress develops, how to project resources through recovery and wind-down, and how the plan links to the firm's internal capital and liquidity adequacy assessment.
objectives: Project capital and liquidity through a stress scenario and wind-down period
Identify sources of liquidity strain, including margin calls, client outflows and trapped cash
Link wind-down resource needs to the firm's internal adequacy assessment
syllabus: Liquidity forecasting, buffers and contingency funding
Capital depletion, losses and the timing of breaches
Estimating wind-down costs and the resources to hold against them
Integrating recovery and wind-down with internal capital and liquidity assessments

modules.title: Solvent Wind-Down: Mechanics, Timeline and Costs
modules.summary: The practical steps to close a business in an orderly way: deciding when to switch from recovery to wind-down, sequencing activities, managing counterparties and staff, and communicating with stakeholders.
objectives: Define the point at which the firm moves from recovery to wind-down
Build a realistic wind-down timeline and sequence of actions
Plan communication with clients, counterparties, staff and supervisors
syllabus: Wind-down triggers and the decision-making process
Closing positions, transferring clients and terminating contracts
Staff retention, key person risk and incentives during wind-down
Stakeholder and supervisor communication plans

modules.title: Returning Client Money and Assets
modules.summary: How to ensure client money, safeguarded funds and client assets, including crypto-assets, can be identified, reconciled and returned promptly in a wind-down or failure.
objectives: Assess the quality of segregation, safeguarding and records for client money and assets
Plan the identification, reconciliation and return of client holdings
Identify shortfall risks and how to prevent them
syllabus: Client money, safeguarding and custody arrangements across sectors
Reconciliation, books and records and resolution packs
Return mechanics: transfer, distribution and unclaimed balances
Crypto-asset custody: keys, wallets and returning digital assets

modules.title: Operational Continuity and Critical Services
modules.summary: Keeping the firm operating long enough to recover or wind down: identifying critical services, people, systems and suppliers, and making contracts and data resilient to a crisis.
objectives: Identify critical services and the resources needed to deliver them in stress
Assess contracts with outsourcers and group entities for continuity in wind-down
Align recovery and wind-down planning with operational resilience and business continuity
syllabus: Mapping critical services, people, systems and data
Third-party and intragroup contracts: termination rights and continuity clauses
Access to systems and records after staff and supplier departures
Links to business continuity and operational resilience frameworks

modules.title: Governance, Testing and Supervisory Review
modules.summary: Brings the programme together: who owns and approves the plan, how it is tested through fire drills and crisis simulation, and how supervisors review plans and what they challenge.
objectives: Define plan ownership, board approval and review cycles
Design fire drills and crisis simulations that test the plan in practice
Anticipate supervisory challenge and evidence the plan's credibility
syllabus: Roles of the board, senior management and control functions
Fire drills, desk-top exercises and lessons-learned logs
How supervisors review plans: common findings and red flags
Workshop: crisis simulation and plan improvement actions

related.title: Engaging Effectively with Your Supervisor: How Firms Are Assessed
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how supervisors assess business models, governance and risk, so they can see themselves as the supervisor does and engage with confidence.

related.title: Fit and Proper for Firms: Appointing and Assessing Key Function Holders
related.summary: A nine-module programme showing firms how to appoint and assess key function holders, prepare applications and interviews, and manage fitness and certification on an ongoing basis.

related.title: Governance Reviews and Supervisory Interviews: Preparing Your Board and Management
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors assess governance and interview directors and staff, and how licensees can evidence effective governance and prepare openly.

related.title: Regulatory Investigations and Enforcement: Responding as a Firm
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement, from first information request to settlement.

related.title: Regulatory Readiness: Authorisation and Supervisory Engagement
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking firms from licence application through to established supervision, showing how authorities assess applications and supervise new firms.

related.title: Supervisory Findings and Remediation: From Risk Assessment to Closure
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors reach findings and how licensees can respond with remediation that fixes root causes and closes issues on evidence.
